q: What is an ATS for in an electrical system?
o: A switch used with a standby generator
An emergency switch in fire alarms
A switch for elevators and conveyors
n: It transfers load between utility and generator.

q: When is the Certificate of Electrical Inspection (CEI) issued?
o: Before the utility installs the meter
After the utility installs the meter
Before the Building Official's final inspection
After the Building Official's final inspection
n: The utility needs the CEI before it energizes and meters the service.

q: What frequency does MERALCO supply to consumers?
n: The Philippine grid runs at 60 Hz.

q: In a string of bulbs wired in series, what happens if one bulb is removed?
o: Only the bulb before it goes out
Only bulbs after it go out
n: A series circuit has a single path.

q: What device detects ground faults and cuts power immediately to prevent shock?
n: A GFCI trips on leakage current.

q: What are the conductors from a main distribution center to the branch-circuit panels called?
n: Feeders supply panelboards.

q: What resists the flow of electricity?
n: Insulators have high resistance.

q: What conductors run from the service equipment to distribution points in a building?
n: Feeders run between the service and the panels.

q: A valve controls water flow. What does the same job in an electrical circuit?
n: A switch opens and closes the circuit.

q: What matters most when sizing wire for a circuit?
n: Wire must carry the load current safely.

q: Power was cut but restored right away by standby generators. What switched the source automatically?
n: An ATS starts and transfers to the generator.

q: What do banks use to bridge the gap before emergency power takes over?
n: A UPS gives instant, unbroken power.

q: What is the main function of an automatic transfer switch?
o: Switching automatically from the utility to a standby generator
n: It senses outage and transfers load.

q: What is the main purpose of a UPS?
o: Temporary power during outages or until a generator starts
n: Batteries carry the load through the gap.

q: In manual emergency switching, what device connects the load to the alternate source?
n: MTS is a manual transfer switch.

q: THHN wire is used for 600 V AC distribution in dry and damp locations. THHN stands for:
n: T-HH-N: thermoplastic, high heat, nylon.

q: THWN stands for:
n: T-H-W-N: thermoplastic, heat, water, nylon.

q: Why do THHN and THWN wires have a nylon jacket?
n: Nylon resists abrasion when pulled through conduit.

q: What color is a ground wire in residential wiring?
n: Green (or green-yellow) or bare marks grounding.

q: What is conduit for?
n: Conduit encloses and protects conductors.

q: What nominal voltage and frequency are used in the Philippines?
n: Supply is 230 V nominal (often called 220 V) at 60 Hz.

q: Which is a brand of electrical wire?
n: Phelps Dodge is a major wire maker.

q: What box holds wire splices and is meant to be concealed and tamper-resistant?
n: Splices are made in junction boxes.

q: What shape is a typical junction box for ceiling outlets?
n: Octagonal boxes are standard for lighting.

q: Which of these is NOT a protective electrical device?
n: CATV is cable television.

q: On which appliance's energy label is the Energy Efficiency Factor (EEF) shown?
n: Philippine labels rate refrigerators by EEF and ACs by EER/CSPF.

q: What is a flat silicon cell that turns sunlight into electricity?
n: PV cells generate current from light.

q: Which is NOT a standard fluorescent lamp wattage?
n: Linear tubes come in 18/20, 36/40 W and similar.

q: To control one light from four locations, what switches are needed?
n: Each location past the two ends adds one 4-way switch.

q: Which switch has a pilot light so it can be found in the dark?
n: Illuminated switches have a built-in indicator.

q: What lighting emphasizes a specific area or object for drama?
n: Accent lighting sets up a focal point.

q: What lighting suits a curved or wavy ceiling?
o: Indirect lighting at the base of the curve
n: Uplight washes reveal the form.

q: What lighting is used for reading at night?
n: Reading needs localized light.

q: What lighting suits a reading desk?
n: A desk lamp is task lighting.

q: What lighting draws attention to an object or casts decorative patterns on a surface?
n: Accent light is directional and focused.

q: Which of these saves up to about 75–80% energy compared with incandescent and gives bright light?
n: CFLs use roughly a quarter of the power.

q: What focuses or intensifies the direction of light?
n: Reflectors redirect light into a beam.

q: What light color is generally preferred in offices for alertness?
n: Cooler light supports alertness.

q: What does a diffuser in a luminaire do?
n: Diffusers scatter light and cut glare.

q: Which lamp has a filament?
n: Incandescents heat a tungsten filament.

q: Which lamp is efficient and long-lived but has no filament?
n: LEDs are solid-state.

q: In office electrical systems, UPS stands for:
n: A UPS supplies battery power.

q: What voltage serves general-purpose office outlets in the Philippines?
n: Local outlets are 230 V (often called 220 V).

q: What starts and runs a compact fluorescent lamp?
n: CFLs have a built-in electronic ballast.

q: What powers and controls an LED lamp?
n: Drivers supply regulated DC.

q: What light is best for reading and writing?
n: Daylight tones aid visual tasks.

q: What is one disadvantage of LED lighting?
n: LEDs cost more up front.

q: What commonly replaces older lamps in street lighting?
n: LEDs are now standard for streets.
